newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's assigns Ba3 rating to Mycal long-term debt.
newsitem.headline: Moody's assigns Ba3 rating to Mycal long-term debt.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday that it had assigned a Ba3 rating to the senior unsecured long-term debt of Mycal Corp.
Moody's said in a statement it was the first time it had rated the debt of the company, a supermarket chain operator.
The Ba3 ratings were assigned to Mycal's unsecured straight bonds as follows:
- Thirty billion yen 5.5 percent Eurobond due 1998
- Series 3 10 billion yen 3.1 percent domestic bonds due 2005
- Series 4 30 billion yen 4.0 percent dual currency domestic bonds due 2005
- Series 5 30 billion yen 2.75 percent domestic bonds due 2002
- Series 6 10 billion yen 2.4 percent domestic bonds due 2001
- Series 7 10 billion yen 2.65 percent domestic bonds due 2002
- Series 8 10 billion yen 2.95 percent domestic bonds due 2003
- Series 9 20 billion yen 3.15 percent domestic bonds due 2004
- Series 10 10 billion yen 3.4 percent domestic bonds due 2006
- Series 11 10 billion yen 2.7 percent domestic bonds due 2002
- Series 12 10 billion yen 3.4 percent domestic bonds due 2006
Moody's said it recognised Mycal's strategy of developing new retailing formats was a response to changes in consumption patterns in Japan.

Nonetheless, it said, the rating took into account the likelihood that Mycal's highly leveraged financial position would be sustained and the business risks arising from operating a highly competitive sector.
